text:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: high 5xx rate on /v1/generate (us-east-1 model-runners). Alert: 5xx_rate > 10% over 4m.

lina_oncall: I'm on the pager, taking lead. Starting live triage.

raj_infra: confirming metric spike on cluster us-east-1a. 5xx peaked at 21% at 2026-04-02T14:12Z. p50 steady, p95 latency doubled.

toni_backend: logs show repeated segfaults and OOM kills from model-worker pods on runner-7 and runner-9. sample:```
Apr 02 14:10:59 runner-7 model_worker[22345]: runtime: panic: runtime error: invalid memory address
Apr 02 14:10:59 runner-7 systemd[1]: model-worker.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=139
Apr 02 14:11:02 runner-9 kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 33445 (model_worker) total-vm:620000kB, anon-rss:500000kB
```

lee_sre: node-level metrics show sustained RSS growth and high page-in activity. Swap used briefly. Candidate root: aggressive KV cache growth combined with a recent quantized-attention kernel change.

olivia_cs: reported impact: Customer Nimbus saw elevated error rate on their /chat endpoint (prod) for ~7 minutes, filed internal ticket. CSM alerted.

lina_oncall: immediate mitigations: 1) enable short-circuit routing for long-sequence requests to a CPU-optimized fallback; 2) temporarily throttle concurrent seq_len>2048 requests at edge; 3) cordon affected nodes and evict pods for safe restart; 4) roll back the last kernel change if crashes persist. Implementing now.

toni_backend: patch ready to toggle: `POST /internal/routing/override {"path":"/v1/generate","policy":"cpu-fallback","percent":100,"duration_s":900}`. I'll apply in 30s.

lina_oncall: applied override, response 202. Shifting heavy-seq traffic to cpu-fallback pool (gradual ramp over 60s).

raj_infra: cordoned runner-7 and runner-9, started controlled drain. Evicted pods with grace to capture core dumps: `kubectl annotate pod <pod> debug=core-collect` then delete.

toni_backend: added HTTP filter to reject seq_len>4096 with 413 for now (prevent runaway requests). Deployed edge rule in 15s.

lee_sre: after drains, memory RSS dropped and no new OOMs on the drained nodes. cpu-fallback is handling long sequences but higher latency — acceptable for mitigation. 5xx down to ~2.3% in region.

olivia_cs: Nimbus notified: brief fallback to CPU for long requests, experiencing higher lat but requests successful now. CSM asking for RCA and ETA on fix.

toni_backend: rolling back quant-attn kernel change across us-east-1 pool and rebuilding the model-runner image with reduced KV_CACHE_MAX=1e8 and enabled kvcache-trim-on-allocate=true. Rolling rollout starting.

raj_infra: launching extra smaller instances to absorb load while rollout proceeds. autoscaler bump +2 nodes.

lina_oncall: taking note: collect core dumps + backtraces from runner-7/9 and upload to /s3/incident/3512346789/artifacts. Toni, please ensure symbols included.

toni_backend: cores uploaded. preliminary backtrace points to kv_cache::grow() path and allocator returning NULL under fragmentation. Also saw use-after-free in attention optimizer path in one trace. Patching both.

lee_sre: post-rollout health: no further segfaults, RSS stable, swap inactive. Region 5xx = 0.8% at 14:33Z. P95 latency for chat long requests up ~400ms because of CPU fallback but customer success prefers successful responses.

olivia_cs: Nimbus CSM acknowledges update. They request ETA for permanent mitigation and whether we will backfill requests that errored.

lina_oncall: short summary for handoff: root cause = KV cache unbounded growth + allocator fragmentation + recent quant-attn regression -> node memory pressure -> crashes -> 5xx spike. Actions taken = edge throttling, CPU-fallback routing, cordon/drain + core collection, rollback kernel change, image rollout with KV caps and kvcache trim, autoscaler + extra nodes. Status = mitigated. Monitoring for 60m.

toni_backend: follow-ups: land kvcache caps in config, add unit/integration tests for quant-attn path, add allocator stresstest.

raj_infra: infra follow-ups: introduce node oom alert with small window, tune autoscaler thresholds, add a memory-pressure circuit breaker to avoid serving new large requests on pressured nodes.

lee_sre: production postmortem owners: backend-engineering (RCAs & fixes), infra (scaling/alerts), edge (request limits & routing playbook), SRE (core collection + observability).

olivia_cs: I'll coordinate customer comms and share the postmortem draft with Nimbus CSM.

lina_oncall: handing off to next oncall (lee_sre) in 25m. tagging incident for postmortem and customer follow-up. Good work team. :tada:

incident-bot: Incident marked mitigated by lina_oncall at 2026-04-02T14:36:40Z.
